transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Democrats have flipped control of Congress
in yesterday's midterm elections.
They needed four seats in the U.S. Senate.
They've taken at least seven.
Two races have yet to be called.
Democrats needed at least three seats in the House.
They've picked up about two dozen,
with many more House races still uncalled.
NPR's Barbara Sprunt says this means a big change
for Congress next year.
Democrats want to flex those muscles
of the legislative branch once again.
And I think we'll see that happen in two big buckets.
A Democratic Senate majority means massive roadblocks
for confirming President Trump's future cabinet
and judicial nominees, of course,
if there's a Supreme Court vacancy.
And on the House side, you know,
we can expect a lot of investigations.
NPR's Barbara Sprunt reporting.
Democrats swept state races in Texas
in one high-profile race.
Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico won,
breaking a 32 Republican lock on statewide office in Texas.
Houston Public Media's Andrew Schneider reports from Austin.
Talarico invoked the biblical story of David and Goliath,
and he said the lesson of his victory
over Republican Ken Paxton was to always bet on the underdog.
This win is for every Texan
who's ever wondered if anyone is listening.
Talarico defied predictions
of what many thought would be a close race,
beating Paxton by more than 10 percentage points
in nearly a million votes.
For NPR News, I'm Andrew Schneider in Austin.
There were Democratic gains in other state races in Texas.
Ena Hosa defeated incumbent governor Greg Abbott
to become that state's first Latina governor.
In Nevada, Democrat Erin Ford will become
that state's first black governor.
In Georgia, Keisha Lance Bottoms will become that state
and the nation's first female black governor.
And in New Mexico, former Democratic Congresswoman Deb
Holland has become the first female
Native American governor-elect.
From member station KUNM, Jeanette Didios has more.
Holland is a member of the Pueblo of Laguna
and served in Congress, then as U.S. interior secretary
before her landmark win Tuesday night.
-I stand before you as the first Native American woman.
Why is it only about history?
It's about our future.
-Holland pledged to pursue stronger public education,
repair the troubled state child welfare department,
address violent crime in fentanyl,
and expand access to healthcare.
Holland will replace Democratic governor Michelle Luhan Grisham,
who is term-limited on January 1st.
For NPR News, I'm Jeanette Didios in Albuquerque.
-In Florida, Republican Byron Donalds will become
that state's first-ever black governor.
This is NPR.
Investors seem very buoyed by the midterm election results.
On Wall Street, in pre-market trading,
the Dow Jones Industrial Average is up more than 760 points,
or about 1.5%.
Both the tech-heavy NASDAQ and the broader S&P 500 indices
are up by about 1%.
One of Colorado's deeply Republican
and rural congressional districts
could choose a Democratic representative.
Colorado Public Radio's Steena Sieg has more.
-At Democrat Dwayne Romero's lively watch party,
he thanked his staff and supporters.
-And all the folks across this entire district
who gave us a shot, you know, gave us a chance.
-The 3rd congressional district is represented by Jeff Herd,
whose event was more subdued
after big Democratic wins nationwide.
Herd told supporters no matter his race as a result.
-I'm proud of the work that we've done,
and I'm proud of the trust
that people have placed in me and in us.
-Republicans have represented the district for the past 15 years.
For NPR News, I'm Steena Sieg in Grand Junction, Colorado.
-In Europe, investigators have not been able to find
who hacked into supermarket freezers and refrigerators
in several countries in Europe this week.
The saboteurs boosted the heat in the fridges and freezers,
often to more than 120 degrees.
Spoiled food had to be thrown out,
costing grocers millions of dollars.
It's the second time this has happened recently.
It's NPR.

topics.text: Democrats flip control of Congress in midterm elections, with Senate and House gains
Democrat James Talarico wins Texas Senate race, beating Republican Ken Paxton by over 10 points
Democrats win Texas state races, including Ena Hosa defeating Governor Greg Abbott
Erin Ford becomes Nevada's first Black governor after winning state election
Keisha Lance Bottoms becomes Georgia's first female Black governor
Deb Haaland becomes New Mexico's first Native American female governor-elect
Byron Donalds becomes Florida's first Black governor after Republican win
Wall Street rallies in pre-market trading after midterm election results
Colorado's 3rd congressional district race between Democrat Dwayne Romero and Republican Jeff Hurd
Saboteurs hack supermarket freezers and fridges across Europe, spoiling food and costing millions
